title: Release Helmsman — Quick Dial & Emergency Retreat Hub
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design a compact, single-pane Rollouts command center — the 'Helmsman' — that surfaces fast exposure controls (Quick Dial), an immediate emergency retreat action (Escape Hub), real-time signal risk ribbon, and a scenario simulator for safe previews. This ticket covers exploration artifacts, a high-fidelity prototype for stakeholder review, and handoff notes for engineering. Objectives: 1) reduce time-to-safe-rollback for on-call engineers to <30s; 2) make canary/A-B traffic adjustments discoverable and reversible; 3) provide an accurate preview of user-visible exposure across cohorts; 4) integrate telemetry links to tracing and cost impact estimates.
ux_highlights: Quick Dial: single control with coarse exponential steps (0.1%, 1%, 5%, 10%, 25%, 50%, 100%) plus fine adjustment modifier
Escape Hub: one-click snapshot + immediate partial rollback to last-known-good variant with visual confirmation and undo window
Signal Ribbon: condensed telemetry strip showing latency, error rate, and policy-triggered risk bands aligned to SLO thresholds
Scenario Simulator: shadow traffic replay slider to preview percent exposure and estimated cost delta
Keyboard shortcuts for rapid exposure changes and emergency retreat (accessible via ? help modal)
Compact confirmation microcopy and progressive disclosure to keep the primary canvas uncluttered
acceptance_criteria: Prototype handed off and reviewed in design critique with PM and two eng leads
Clickable Figma prototype demonstrates Quick Dial, Escape Hub, Signal Ribbon, and Scenario Simulator flows
Design tokens and component specs captured for dev (CSS variables, accessible color contrast ratios, motion guidelines)
Handoff includes a prioritized list of API endpoints and telemetry events for implementation
Usability checklist completed with 6 internal testers and recorded task success rates >=90% for rollback flows
updates: 2025-02-15 Ava Martinez: Initial discovery complete. Interviewed two SREs and three PMs. Top risk is accidental over-exposure during rapid adjustments. Proposed Quick Dial with modifier keys to prevent overshoot.
2025-02-17 Liam Chen: Built low-fi flows for Quick Dial and Escape Hub; added a visual lock state when rollout is linked to autoscaling policy. Requesting a small usability test with on-call team.
2025-02-18 PM review (Jordan Patel): Asked for cost preview integration and an explicitly-labeled 'Preview only' toggle for shadow replays. Added label to backlog for telemetry events.

2025-02-19 Design critique: consensus to prioritize Escape Hub first for MVP. Decided to defer cohort-targeting matrix to a follow-up ticket. Feedback: make emergency action reversible for 2 minutes with clear undo affordance.
2025-02-20 Liam Chen: High-fidelity prototype uploaded to Figma and live prototype endpoints wired for demo. Preparing engineering handoff doc and component inventory.
2025-02-20 Ava Martinez: Requested security review before handoff; flagged as not required for UI-only changes but included telemetry event contract for compliance review.
design_notes: Prefer exponential steps for first-release to reduce accidental linear drift when responding to incidents.
Escape Hub should create a deterministic snapshot object referenced by the rollback API (snapshot id visible in UI).
Telemetry ribbon uses color semantics aligned to alerting standards: green/amber/red, with hover to show exact metric values and links to traces.
Cost preview shows incremental cost per 1 minute at current QPS and estimated 24h delta at selected exposure.
Mobile layout: collapse Quick Dial into an overflow action and surface Escape Hub as sticky FAB in narrow screens.
